walkthroughs.body_html: Ossification turns cartilage into bone during childhood. Adolescents have growth plates that close in early 20s. Weight-bearing exercise builds bone density, peaking around age 30, then slowly declining.
Osteoporosis reduces bone density, raising fracture risk — especially hips, wrists and spine. Prevention: weight-bearing exercise, calcium-rich diet and vitamin D. Common after menopause in women.

Good posture stacks the spine, reducing back pain. Strong core muscles and balanced training prevent issues like kyphosis (rounded upper back) or lordosis (over-arched lower back), which can plague desk-bound students and athletes alike.
